name: Tjibaou Cultural Centre (ADCK)
funding: Operating budget about 400M XPF (~US$3.6M) in 2026. Run by the public agency ADCK; the French State pays 68% of a 405M XPF renovation (2025).

name: Artspace Aotearoa
funding: Creative New Zealand (NZ$637k a year for 2027 to 2029) and Auckland Council lead; strategic partners are Chartwell Trust, Foundation North, Goethe-Institut and Wesfarmers.

name: Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki
funding: Run by Tātaki Auckland Unlimited for Auckland Council. Partners include BMW, Van Cleef & Arpels, HSBC, Anthony Harper and Baker Tilly. Trusts include Chartwell and Mackelvie.

name: Te Uru Waitakere Contemporary Gallery
funding: Core funding from the Waitākere Ranges Local Board (Auckland Council). It also takes gifts from a Benefactors Collective and sponsors, none named.

name: Christchurch Art Gallery
funding: Christchurch City Council; the Christchurch Art Gallery Foundation raises acquisition funds. Partners are JBWere (foundation partner) and Anthony Harper (major partner), plus hotel, design and drinks suppliers.

name: Dunedin Public Art Gallery
funding: Dunedin City Council gallery. Gallery Partners are Creative New Zealand, Quartz Reef and Craigs Investment Partners; the DPAG Society buys works.

name: The Dowse Art Museum
funding: Mostly funded by Hutt City Council, plus the Dowse Foundation; Jan 2025 archive names Dulux as a corporate partner and Steel & Tube as a donor.

name: Enjoy Contemporary Art Space
funding: Creative New Zealand Arts Council Toi Aotearoa is its primary funder, with additional support from Wellington City Council.

name: Te Papa
funding: NZ$85M revenue (2024-25), Crown 52%. Its current partners page lists Panasonic, Bloomberg, Samsung, MyLotto and gaming-machine trusts PubCharity and Lion Foundation.

name: Toi Māori Aotearoa
funding: Small charitable trust. Major funder is Creative New Zealand (government and Lotteries money). Runs the Toi Māori Gallery.
